earlier_scan.source_named: Rapoisi/Konua (Bougainville): Muller 1954, Grammar and Vocabulary of the Konua Language (Micro-Bibliotheca Anthropos); Robinson 2011 discusses subgrouping; no online copy reachable.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Rapoisi language' (raw wikitext and revision history, 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Consonant/vowel tables and a 14-letter orthography, added 2024-06-16 by user SfindIrshAp with no citation; nothing on stress. Not usable as a source.

sources.citation: Robinson, Stuart P. 2011. Split intransitivity in Rotokas, a Papuan language of Bougainville. PhD, Radboud Universiteit Nijmegen.
sources.note: Phonology chapter is about Rotokas only. pp. 247-248 (sect. 11.1.3): Konua is 'the only language in the Rotokas family that has been described in print... thanks to the vocabulary and grammatical notes of Muller (1954)'; cites Müller 1954: 73/107 for verb agreement. Nothing on Konua stress.

sources.citation: Regan, Anthony J. & Helga M. Griffin (eds.). 2005. Bougainville before the conflict. Canberra: ANU Press (incl. D. Tryon, The languages of Bougainville).
sources.note: Nothing; Kunua (Konua) appears only in language lists and population tables (3,500 speakers, 1998).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1977. Institutional framework of language study: Anthropos Institute. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 3 (Pacific Linguistics C-40), 1317-1340.
sources.note: Nothing; lists Burgmann 1954a (Anthropos 49: 295-8) as the introduction to Müller's Konua manuscript in the Micro-Bibliotheca Anthropos.

sources.citation: Wurm, S. A. 1975. The East Papuan Phylum in general. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 783-804.
sources.note: p. 796 (Bougainville Stock, North group incl. Konua): 'in Rotokas at least, there is a complex suprasegmental phonology in which length and stress patterns play a part.' Konua is mentioned only for inclusive/exclusive pronouns and possessive suffixes; nothing on Konua stress.

sources.citation: Burgmann, Arnold. 1954. A. Müllers Grammatik und Vokabular der Konua-Sprache. Anthropos 49: 295-298.
sources.note: Nothing. Summarises Müller's MBA 12 typescript: 'Grammatical Notes on the Konua Language' (24 pp.) plus 'Dictionary Konua-English' (88 pp., c. 1220 entries); p. 297: 'Die "Grammatical Notes" sind kurz und skizzenhaft gehalten... Es werden behandelt: Zahlwörter, Artikel, Nomen, Adjektiv, Adverb, Pronomen, Konjugation des Verbum, Präpositionen und Konjunktionen.' No phonology mentioned.

sources.citation: Müller, Adam. 1954. Grammar and Vocabulary of the Konua Language (Grammatical Notes on the Konua Language, 24 pp. typescript + Dictionary Konua-English, 88 pp.). Micro-Bibliotheca Anthropos 12. Posieux (Fribourg): Anthropos-Institut.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only first-hand description of Konua/Rapoisi (Glottolog MED; source for WALS, Grambank, ASJP). Burgmann's summary lists no phonology section, so the chance of a stress statement is modest, but the vocabulary may carry accent marks. Harvard holds the microfilm: TOZ Microfilm L.SOC.12.70.6.13 (12); OCLC 702439392.
